title: "Statistics Skills Practice"

This page generates practice questions. It is for
practising calculations and procedures, choosing the right formula, standardising, using the Z-table, $t$-table and doing the arithmetic. This does not generate or practice conceptual questions.

How it works:

- choose a **seed** (any whole number), a **difficulty**, the number of  **questions** and which **topics** to include;
- press **Generate practice set**;
- Use the formula sheet ([link](https://vandenman.github.io/stats12/2627/misc/formula_sheet/formula_sheet.html)) for equations, z and $t$-tables.
- type your answer in the box and press **Check answer**;
- if you are stuck, ask for a **hint**, or open the **worked solution**.

The questions are generated from the seed: the same seed with the same settings always gives exactly the same set of questions. So you can write down "seed 18492, difficulty 2, question 4" and come back to that question later. Generate as many sets as you like. No data is saved or sent anywhere.

## Generate a practice set

<div class="practice-controls">
  <p>
    <label>Seed: <input id="practice-seed" type="number" value="1234" step="1" size="8"></label>
    <label>Difficulty:
      <select id="practice-difficulty">
        <option value="1">1 - one step</option>
        <option value="2">2 - two steps</option>
        <option value="3">3 - work backwards</option>
      </select>
    </label>
    <label>Questions:
      <select id="practice-n">
        <option value="5">5</option>
        <option value="10" selected>10</option>
        <option value="15">15</option>
      </select>
    </label>
  </p>
  <p>Topics:
    <label><input id="practice-probability" type="checkbox" checked> Probability Theory</label>
    <label><input id="practice-Z" type="checkbox" checked> Z-test</label>
    <label><input id="practice-t" type="checkbox" checked> t-test</label>
    <label><input id="practice-normal" type="checkbox" checked> Normal distribution</label>
    <label><input id="practice-clt" type="checkbox" checked> Central limit theorem</label>
    <label><input id="practice-bayes" type="checkbox" checked> Bayes theorem</label>
  </p>
  <p><button id="practice-generate" type="button">Generate practice set</button></p>
</div>

<p id="practice-status"><em>Starting R&hellip;</em></p>

<div id="practice-output"></div>

<script>
// Page logic.  This only reads the form and shows what R sends back: the
// questions, the answers and the grading all come from the R functions
// further down the page.
(function () {
  "use strict";

  const output = document.getElementById("practice-output");
  const status = document.getElementById("practice-status");
  let webR = null;   // the R session, once the module script below has it

  // A JavaScript string written as R source.  JSON escaping is close enough
  // to R's own for the values we pass across.
  const rString = (text) => JSON.stringify(text);

  // The current settings, read straight off the form.
  const settings = () => {
    const topics = [];
    if (document.getElementById("practice-probability").checked) topics.push("probability");
    if (document.getElementById("practice-Z").checked) topics.push("Z");
    if (document.getElementById("practice-t").checked) topics.push("t");
    if (document.getElementById("practice-normal").checked) topics.push("normal");
    if (document.getElementById("practice-clt").checked) topics.push("clt");
    if (document.getElementById("practice-bayes").checked) topics.push("bayes");
    return {
      seed: Number(document.getElementById("practice-seed").value),
      difficulty: Number(document.getElementById("practice-difficulty").value),
      n_questions: Number(document.getElementById("practice-n").value),
      topics: topics
    };
  };

  // Show an error rather than leaving the page stuck.
  const showError = (error) => {
    output.innerHTML = "";
    const pre = document.createElement("pre");
    pre.className = "pq-error";
    pre.textContent = String(error);
    output.appendChild(pre);
  };

  // Generate a set.
  const generate = async () => {
    if (webR === null) {
      output.innerHTML = "<p><strong>R is still starting up.</strong></p>";
      return;
    }
    const chosen = settings();
    if (chosen.topics.length === 0) {
      output.innerHTML = "<p><strong>Tick at least one topic.</strong></p>";
      return;
    }
    output.innerHTML = "<p><em>Generating&hellip;</em></p>";
    try {
      const call =
        "practice_html(" +
        chosen.seed + ", " + chosen.n_questions + ", " + chosen.difficulty + ", c(" +
        chosen.topics.map(rString).join(", ") + "))";
      output.innerHTML = await webR.evalRString(call);
    } catch (error) {
      showError(error);
    }
  };

  // One click handler for the whole set: check an answer, show a hint, show
  // the worked solution.
  output.addEventListener("click", async (event) => {
    const button = event.target;
    const question = button.closest(".pq-question");
    if (!question) return;

    if (button.classList.contains("pq-hint-button")) {
      const box = question.querySelector(".pq-hint");
      box.hidden = !box.hidden;
      button.textContent = box.hidden ? "Show hint" : "Hide hint";
      return;
    }

    if (button.classList.contains("pq-solution-button")) {
      const box = question.querySelector(".pq-solution");
      box.hidden = !box.hidden;
      button.textContent = box.hidden ? "Show worked solution" : "Hide worked solution";
      return;
    }

    if (button.classList.contains("pq-check")) {
      const input = question.querySelector(".pq-answer");
      const feedback = question.querySelector(".pq-feedback");
      feedback.textContent = "Checking...";
      try {
        feedback.textContent = await webR.evalRString(
          "check_answer_text(" + rString(input.value) + ", " +
          Number(input.dataset.correct) + ", " + Number(input.dataset.tolerance) + ")"
        );
        feedback.className = feedback.textContent === "Correct!"
          ? "pq-feedback pq-correct"
          : "pq-feedback pq-wrong";
      } catch (error) {
        showError(error);
      }
    }
  });

  document.getElementById("practice-generate").addEventListener("click", generate);

  // The module script below calls one of these once R is running (or has
  // failed to start).
  window.practiceReady = (instance) => {
    webR = instance;
    status.textContent = "R is running. Choose your settings and press \u201cGenerate practice set\u201d.";
  };
  window.practiceFailed = (error) => {
    status.innerHTML = "<strong>R could not be started:</strong> " + String(error);
  };
})();
</script>

<script type="module">
// R in the browser.  webR is a WebAssembly build of R, loaded from the webR
// project's CDN; this page needs an internet connection for that, and nothing
// else.  (Quarto Live's own live-html format cannot be used here, because the
// OJS runtime it is built on refuses to start from file:// URLs.)
import { WebR } from "https://webr.r-wasm.org/v0.6.0/webr.mjs";

try {
  const webR = new WebR({ baseUrl: "https://webr.r-wasm.org/v0.6.0/" });
  await webR.init();

  // The R functions are the contents of the files in R/, bundled into this
  // page as one hidden code block further down; read it back and evaluate it.
  const rCode = document.querySelector(".practice-source code").textContent;
  await webR.evalRVoid(rCode);

  window.practiceReady(webR);
} catch (error) {
  window.practiceFailed(error);
}
</script>


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

# Emit one hidden code block holding every R helper file, in load order.
helper_files <- c(
  "R/utils.R", "R/probability.R", "R/normal.R", "R/clt.R", "R/bayes.R",
  "R/ztests.R", "R/ttests.R", "R/generators.R"
)

cat("::: {.practice-source}\n\n```\n")
for (file in helper_files) {
  cat(paste(readLines(file), collapse = "\n"), "\n")
}
cat("```\n\n:::\n")
```
